reasons: The excerpt supports that the speaker's organization performs the listed analyses and creates roadmaps/frameworks for Ezra's brands.

However, the high-volume sentence immediately follows the discussion of cross-functional teamwork, so its referent is not clearly the full data stack. The candidate title and claim attach the high-volume qualifier to the organization’s full-data-stack work without clear support.

The source explicitly recommends funnel and drop-off analysis, says full GA or tracking-software analysis is not needed under 300,000 sessions, and directs analysis of both where users drop off and why.
It also conditionally identifies PDP, cart, checkout, thank-you page, and applicable upsells for an ad-to-PDP funnel.
The source says everyone should install a heat map on the product page, using 10,000 and 10 million monthly sessions as illustrative traffic levels.
It explicitly directs analysis of clicks, scrolling, and scroll depth, and the candidate preserves the tool caveats as source-attributed statements.
The source defines false/rage clicks as clicks on elements styled like buttons or links that are not interactive and says to look into them.
It reports that eliminating false clicks has produced uplifts and wins in high-volume stores; the candidate does not turn that experience report into a numerical or universal performance guarantee.
The source calls post-purchase surveys non-negotiable and expressly instructs asking at least the two stated questions.
The candidate appropriately flags the recommended-tool wording as transcription-ambiguous rather than certifying a specific product name.
The CSV-to-GPT/AI review-mining process and the requested outputs are supported.

The source qualifies the recommendation with the disfluent volume wording "if you have over, you know, 500, a thousand reviews." Although the candidate notes this uncertainty in its claim and unknowns, its trigger requires only that reviews exist. Revise the applicability condition to retain the source's large-review-volume qualification without inventing a precise threshold.

The source supports combining qualitative and quantitative data to understand what is happening and why, then using it for landing pages, offer/price testing, or, for bigger stores, comprehensive A/B testing at velocity.

The candidate makes "Do both data types in full" a universal instruction. Elsewhere in the excerpt, the source distinguishes stores over 300,000 sessions, which should do all listed work, from stores under that level, which should focus on bolded items. The candidate should preserve this traffic-volume qualification or identify the tension rather than flattening it.
In the qualitative-data section, the source says stores over 300,000 sessions should do all of the listed work as a non-negotiable and says stores below that level should focus on the bolded items.
The candidate retains the lack of a stated session period and the ambiguity of "all of this."
The warning is directly supported by the source statement that many brands hide important information below the fold.
The source directly reports examples of exit-pop or cookie-modal bugs appearing above a product-page CTA, as well as cookie bars overlaying cart buttons.
The source does state that Clarity is free and laggy and presents heatmap.com as tracking revenue rather than only clicks.

The source also immediately discloses that heatmap.com belongs to "one of my partners." The candidate omits that material qualification while presenting the tool assessment as an independent comparison.
The agency-only condition, over-300,000-session condition, two-to-three-week duration, approximate 100-page document, and partial list of findings are all present in the excerpt.

However, the prerequisite converts the transcription wording "whenever you work with us on the higher side" into a definite "higher service tier." That interpretation is not established by the excerpt and should be preserved as ambiguous.
The speaker explicitly says, "I would install clarity by Microsoft," while noting that it is free, not the best, and laggy.
The candidate does not invent setup requirements or performance thresholds.
The source presents heatmap.com as a heatmap option and attributes its claimed distinction to revenue-based rather than click-only tracking.
It also says the product belongs to "one of my partners." The candidate should include that source-stated affiliation when relaying the positive recommendation.
The source explicitly characterizes qualitative data as explaining why people act and gives surveys, post-purchase feedback, and usability testing as examples.

source_limitations: The excerpt begins mid-sentence and ends mid-sentence, so surrounding context and the remainder of the agency-audit findings are unavailable.
The transcript contains ambiguous or likely mistranscribed terms, including "G4," "no commerce, Komerse," "higher side," and "heruristic."
The excerpt refers to items being bolded as non-negotiables, but formatting is not available in the supplied plain text; the full set of bolded items cannot be determined reliably.

The 300,000-session threshold is stated, but its measurement period is not stated. The source also does not define "high volume," "bigger store," or what it means to perform either data type "in full."
Tool capabilities and tool-quality statements are speaker assertions in the excerpt, not independently demonstrated evidence; heatmap.com is explicitly associated with one of the speaker's partners.
